s.t:
Was wir suchen
Jedes Unternehmen braucht laufend neue Kunden – und genau dieses Problem lösen wir. Mit Interlead bauen die #1 Plattform für Leads, Termine und Aufträge und machen die Kundengewinnung für unsere Partner damit einfacher, transparenter und planbarer.
Zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt suchen wir daher einen Product Owner (m/w/d) für unser Tech Team (hybrid/remote).
Das sind deine Aufgaben
Du übernimmst die Verantwortung für die kontinuierliche Weiterentwicklung unserer Lead-Matching-Software – unserer eigens entwickelten Kernanwendung zur automatisierten Neukundengewinnung.
Du sorgst dafür, dass die Entwicklung reibungslos voranschreitet und unsere Entwickler jederzeit an den richtigen Prioritäten arbeiten.
Du konzipierst eigenständig neue Features, nimmst Anforderungen aus den Fachabteilungen und von Usern auf und übersetzt sie in klare Arbeitspakete (z. B. Tickets, Mockups etc.).
Du prüfst neue Features auf Funktionalität und Qualität, begleitest den Release-Prozess und verantwortest den Live-Gang.
Du bist die Schnittstelle zwischen I T, Fachabteilungen und externen Dienstleistern und sorgst während des gesamten Entwicklungsprozesses für eine transparente Kommunikation.
Du hältst alle relevanten Stakeholder regelmäßig über den aktuellen Entwicklungsstand auf dem Laufenden.
Du identifizierst, konzipierst und implementierst AI-Anwendungen , die unsere Softwarelösungen und internen Prozesse intelligenter und effizienter machen – von der ersten Idee bis zum produktiven Einsatz.
Dank deiner Expertise erreichst du folgende Meilensteine bei uns

Du lernst die Leadbase (Matching, Dialer, Partner-Portal, Versand & Abrechnung sowie APIs) und die wichtigsten Stakeholder aus Vertrieb, Operations und Tech kennen.
Du übernimmst die Pflege des Backlogs sowie die laufende Priorisierung der Tickets im Tech-Team.
Du setzt erste kleinere Verbesserungen eigenständig um – von der Anforderungsaufnahme über die Qualitätssicherung bis zum Live-Gang.
Du etablierst regelmäßige Kommunikationsformate (z. B. wöchentliche Status-Updates oder Release Notes) und hältst Fachabteilungen sowie Management über den Entwicklungsstand auf dem Laufenden.

Du verantwortest eigenständig ein größeres Feature oder eine Produktinitiative der Leadbase – von der Konzeption bis zum erfolgreichen Rollout.
Du stehst im regelmäßigen Austausch mit den Fachbereichen und priorisierst Anforderungen nach ihrem Nutzen und ihrer Relevanz.
Du identifizierst konkrete Einsatzmöglichkeiten für KI und setzt erste Prozessoptimierungen um (z. B. zur Automatisierung von Anforderungsprozessen oder zur Steigerung der internen Produktivität).

Du gestaltest die Produktstrategie für Lead Matching und angrenzende Module (z. B. Dialer, Multi-Channel und Partner-API) aktiv mit und bringst mindestens ein strategisches Vorhaben erfolgreich in Produktion.
Du hast mindestens eine KI-Lösung erfolgreich produktiv eingeführt.
Du bist die zentrale Ansprechperson für Produktfragen rund um die Leadbase und wirst von Fachabteilungen sowie externen Partnern als verlässliche Schnittstelle wahrgenommen.
Das bringst du mit
Du bringst Erfahrung als Product Owner oder Product Manager in einem agilen Umfeld mit – idealerweise in einem SaaS- oder Tech-Unternehmen.
Du verfügst über ein gutes technisches Verständnis und hast Freude daran, die Brücke zwischen Business und Entwicklung zu schlagen.
Du hast erste Berührungspunkte mit künstlicher Intelligenz oder ein fundiertes Interesse daran, KI-Lösungen praxisnah im Unternehmenskontext einzusetzen.
Du arbeitest strukturiert und proaktiv und kannst komplexe Anforderungen in klare Aufgaben und Prioritäten übersetzen.
Du kommunizierst sicher und verständlich – auch bei technischen Themen und mit unterschiedlichen Stakeholdern.
Du begeisterst dich für datengetriebene, digitale Produkte und hast den Anspruch, Dinge aktiv voranzubringen und nachhaltig zu verbessern.
Das bieten wir dir
Ein dynamisches Marketing- und Tech-Umfeld sowie die Möglichkeit, gemeinsam “The Lead Company” aufzubauen.
Ein riesiger Markt und zahlreiche interne Wachstumsmöglichkeiten – wir lösen das größte Problem unserer Partner: die Automatisierung ihrer Neukundengewinnung.
Volle Flexibilität im Arbeitsort (remote, im Bremer Headquarter oder nach Absprache auch aus dem Ausland).
Volle Flexibilität in der Arbeitszeit – du gestaltest deine Arbeitszeiten individuell mit deinem Team.
30 Tage Urlaub pro Jahr + die Möglichkeit, jederzeit unbezahlten Urlaub zu nehmen.
Zuschuss zur betrieblichen Altersvorsorge (die “Interlead‑Rente”).
Jährliche Teamevents wie Sommerfest & Weihnachtsfeier.
Agiles Arbeitsumfeld – moderne Tools wie Slack, Monday, Notion, Google Workspace und OKRs/Scrum unterstützen dich bei der täglichen Arbeit.
Zuschuss fürs Fitnessstudio (über Urban Sports Club oder E‑Gym Wellpass).
Schnelle Entscheidungen – wir sind 100 % bootstrapped, profitabel und unabhängig von Investoren.
Eine offene Feedback‑Kultur und regelmäßige interne Trainings.
Transparente Kommunikation durch monatliche All‑Hands‑Meetings , wöchentlichen Newsletter und feste Team‑Updates.
Im Headquarter in der Bremer Überseestadt erwarten dich ergonomische Arbeitsplätze, großartiger Kaffee & Espresso, Getränke und Grillabende.
Für Home‑Office‑Mitarbeitende: monatliche Home‑Office‑Pauschale von 20 €.
Bikeleasing, lease dein Wunschfahrrad oder E-Bike zu attraktiven Konditionen.
Das sind unsere Werte
Fail Fast: Wir leben eine ausgeprägte Testing- und Fehlerkultur. Wir sind pragmatisch, mutig und fühlen uns mit Veränderung wohl.
Ergebnisse: Wir arbeiten flexibel, aber verlässlich. Bei uns steht Freiheit in Einklang mit Ergebnisorientierung und Eigenverantwortung.
Vertrauen: Wir gehen offen mit Zahlen, Stärken und Schwächen um und machen das, was für die Firma richtig ist ("Ego zurück").

About Remote Remote is solving modern organizations’ biggest challenge – navigating global employment compliantly with ease. We make it possible for businesses of all sizes to recruit, pay, and manage international teams.

With our core values at heart and future focused work culture, our team works tirelessly on ambitious problems, asynchronously, around the world. You can find Remote rs working from 6 different continents (Antarctica left to go!) and all of our positions are fully remote.

With Innovation as one of the core values, we have built Automation and AI capabilities into the requirements for every role. We encourage every member of the Remote team to bring their talents, experiences and culture to the table to help us build the best-in-class HR platform.

If you are energetic, curious, motivated and ambitious, be part of our world. Apply now and define the future of work! What this job can offer you This is an exciting time to join Remote and make a personal difference in the global employment space as a Product Manager , joining our Product team in the Fintech vertical .

As a Billing Platform Product Manager, you will be a key member of our triad of product managers in the billing team, each leading their independent teams yet working within an interconnected scope. As a Product Manager at Remote , you'll be developing and guiding our strategy for a key product area in Finance.

You'll advance this vision by working with a cross-functional engineering and design group to find our most important problems and shape iterative solutions towards them. What you bring Prior experience as product manager in billing / invoicing or similar, ideally at a high-growth company Proficiency in Cursor and/or Claude Code or similar tool.

You must be able to autonomously build, debug, and ship functional prototypes or small code changes with the help of AI tooling, not just write specs.

Great judgment making both strategic (what to prioritize) and tactical (feature scope) decisions Demonstrable, self-driven results that have moved a product in the right direction A passion for creating seamless and effective products, even when the challenges they address are complex and intricate.

Outstanding communication and collaboration skills, including across different departments (e.g. business operations, sales, etc.) to ensure that we’re satisfying critical business requirements Proficient in English, both written and spoken. Bonus: Experience working in a remote environment.

Key Responsibilities Build solutions together with the rest of the team that solve for finance, billing and other financial services at Remote Own not just software implementation, but the end-to-end experience: Remote delivers value through services powered by both humans and software Lead on complex solutions without requiring support or involvement from senior members of the product team Effectively manage internal expectations for complex projects, products, and features while navigating challenging prioritization decisions Drive Remote in the right direction by building an effective roadmap and strategy for your area of the product in Finance Break down strategic plans into near and mid-term goals that's easy for others to understand Align your product roadmap with higher level department and company problems we’re working to solve Be the subject matter expert for your product area Contribute to scaling and growth plans for your product area Ship improvements quickly and iteratively, challenging yourself and counterparts to find minimal solutions to problems Support and leads a product team delivering high throughput and high return on investment Understand key business KPIs and align your team's work and metrics to directly improve to these Work together with engineers, designers and stakeholders to build solutions to important complex problems Communicate and collaborate internally and externally Contribute to the Product org by sharing your techniques, processes, and learnings Communicate and promote the work of your team and why it matters to customers and internal teams Work asynchronously and transparently Lead on solutions with minimal support or involvement from senior members of the product team.

You should be able to work autonomously on simple features and iterations, only needing support to solve complex problems Contribute to tactical and strategic decision-making for your business area Develop into a subject matter expert for understanding, articulating, and solving complex business problems related to our mobile experiences Practicals You'll report to: Group Product Manager Location : For this position we welcome everyone to apply Start date: As soon as possible Remote Compensation Philosophy Remote 's Total Rewards philosophy is to ensure fair, unbiased compensation and fair equity pay along with competitive benefits in all locations in which we operate.

We do not agree to or encourage cheap-labor practices and therefore we ensure to pay above in-location rates. We hope to inspire other companies to support global talent-hiring and bring local wealth to developing countries. At first glance our salary bands seem quite wide - here is some context.

At Remote we have international operations and a globally distributed workforce. We use geo ranges to consider geographic pay differentials as part of our global compensation strategy to remain competitive in various markets while we hiring globally. The base salary range for this full-time position is $62,400 to $140,400.

Our salary ranges are determined by role, level and location, and our job titles may span more than one career level. The actual base pay for the successful candidate in this role is dependent upon many factors such as location, transferable or job-related skills, work experience, relevant training, business needs, and market demands.

The base salary range may be subject to change. At Remote , we foster internal mobility as a key element of our culture of employee growth and development, supported by a compensation philosophy that guarantees pay equity and fairness.

Therefore, all compensation changes associated with an internal move will be reviewed by the Total Rewards & People Enablement team on a case by case basis.

Agentic AI ist deine Welt – und du willst dich damit beschäftigen, statt ständig etwas verkaufen zu müssen?
Du hast dich intensiv mit KI-Agenten beschäftigt, eigene Workflows oder Anwendungen gebaut und kennst Themen wie n8n, Make, APIs, Tool Calling, RAG, Vektordatenbanken oder MCP aus der Praxis?
Dann bau mit uns den besten Agentic-AI-Kurs im deutschsprachigen Raum.
Aufgaben
Der Titel heißt Product Manager – gemeint ist aber jemand, der Lerninhalte baut, nichtverwaltet: halb Instructional Designer, halb Agentic-AI-Bastler. Du gestaltest das Produkt „Kurs“, von der ersten Demo bis zum fertigen Modul. Dabei beschäftigst du dich mit uns zusammen unter anderem mit folgenden Fragen:
Was müssen Menschen heute über Agentic AI wissen?
Welche Tools, Modelle und Frameworks sind wirklich relevant?
Welche Agenten und Automatisierungen sollten Teil des Kurses sein?
Wie lassen sich technische Inhalte verständlich und praxisnah vermitteln?
Welche Übungen, Projekte und Demos bringen Teilnehmer wirklich weiter?
Du unterstützt uns dabei, Inhalte zu strukturieren, praktische Anwendungen zu bauen, Lernmaterialien zu entwickeln und Referenten fachlich zu begleiten. Einzelne Inhalte kannst du später auch selbst unterrichten.
Qualifikation
Wir suchen keinen Verkäufer und keinen klassischen Bildungsmanager – sondern jemanden mit technischem Hintergrund, der bereits tief in Agentic AI steckt, neue Entwicklungen aufmerksam verfolgt und komplexe Dinge verständlich erklären kann.
Ob Berufseinsteiger mit starkem Portfolio oder mit ein paar Jahren Erfahrung in Content, Training oder Produktentwicklung – entscheidend ist, was du bereits gebaut oder vermittelt hast, nicht dein Titel.

Kleines Team, kurze Wege
Hybrides Arbeits-Setup: Büro in Berlin-Mitte + Homeoffice
Tägliche Arbeit mit den aktuellsten KI-Tools und -Entwicklungen
Echte Verantwortung ab Tag 1 - du verwaltest nicht, du baust auf
Perspektive auf eine wachsende Rolle in einem wachsenden Bereich
Vollzeit, unbefristet.
Schick uns nicht nur deinen Lebenslauf – zeig uns, womit du dich beschäftigst und was du bereits gebaut oder entwickelt hast (z.B. Kurskonzepte, Workshops, Tutorials oder Prototypen)!

We are looking for a Associate Product Delivery Manager to help turn product priorities into clear, well-organized work for our engineering and design teams.
Working closely with our Product Lead, you will help define new features, prepare upcoming work, coordinate requirements, and keep track of sprint progress. You will bring structure and clarity to the product-development process while growing your product-management skills through hands-on experience and mentorship.
This is a good opportunity for someone early in their product career who is organized, curious, and comfortable collaborating across different disciplines.
Tasks
Draft feature scopes, requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria with guidance from the Product Lead.
Help maintain and organize the product backlog.
Prepare features and tasks for refinement and sprint planning.
Coordinate requirements and open questions between product, engineering, and design.
Track sprint status, delivery progress, dependencies, and blockers.
Keep the team and relevant stakeholders informed about progress and changes.
Support planning, refinement, reviews, and other product-delivery meetings.

s.h: Document product requirements, decisions, and changes.
s.t:
Gather the information needed for prioritization discussions.
Contribute recommendations while the Product Lead retains final prioritization responsibility.
Help improve the team’s product-development and delivery processes.
Take on greater product ownership as your skills and experience develop.

Approximately 1–3 years of relevant experience in product management, project coordination, business analysis, software delivery, design, QA, or a related area. Relevant internships and working-student experience may count.
Some experience working with software engineering, design, or other multidisciplinary teams.
The ability to turn discussions and ideas into clear written requirements and action items.
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
Clear and thoughtful written and verbal communication.
Confidence following up on open questions, dependencies, and commitments.
Curiosity about users, technology, and how digital products are built.
A collaborative mindset and willingness to ask questions and learn.
Basic familiarity with agile product development and tools such as Jira, Linear, Notion, or Confluence.
Helpful, but not required
Experience writing user stories or acceptance criteria.
Familiarity with sprint planning, backlog refinement, or software-release processes.
Enough technical curiosity to learn about APIs, data flows, system dependencies, and implementation trade-offs.
Experience working in a startup, scale-up, or another quickly changing environment.
You do not need to meet every item on this list. We care about your potential, judgment, communication skills, and willingness to learn.

s.h: What success looks like within your first six months
s.t:
Upcoming features and tasks are documented clearly and prepared on time.
Sprint progress, dependencies, and blockers are visible to the team.
Product decisions and requirement changes are consistently documented.
Engineering and design know where to find the information they need.
Open questions are identified and brought to the right people early.
The Product Lead has reliable support across planning, prioritization, and delivery.
You begin handling smaller features with increasing independence.

We offer an exciting environment at the interface between IT and entertainment and marketing as part of an ambitious, international and results-orientated team in a young startup.
You work with an excellent international team with varied tasks with a wide range of great opportunities

Monthly learning budget
Urban Sports Club membership support
Support for your favourite means of transport - we help finance your new bike or your public transport subscription
We are a startup in one of the cultural hubs in Berlin, you'll never get bored

Job Description: Associate Product Manager - RHT Marketing ( Solventum ) Solventum , a new healthcare company with a rich history Our company is built on a trusted legacy of solving big healthcare challenges that improve patient lives while enabling healthcare professionals to perform at their best.

People, and their well-being, are at the heart of every scientific advancement we pursue. We partner closely with the best minds in healthcare — guided by empathy, insight, and clinical intelligence — to solve our customers’ toughest challenges. Our ultimate goal? Move humanity forward by improving health for everyone.

Because at Solventum , we never stop solving for you. The impact you’ll make in this role As an Associate Product Manager, you’ll work alongside sharp, inquisitive minds from a wide spectrum of backgrounds and disciplines.

Together, you'll explore new ideas, challenge assumptions, and shape solutions that make a real-world impact by: The RHT franchise is anchored by Restrata® Electrospun Fiber Matrix, a regenerative wound care solution designed to support soft tissue healing.

Restrata became part of Solventum ’s portfolio through the acquisition of Acera Surgical in December 2025.

The APM will execute product and program launch activities, including the development of launch materials, communications, and training programs, while gaining hands-on experience throughout the product development and commercialization process.

This role will also support the coordination of project deliverables across cross-functional teams, including Marketing, Sales, R&D, Clinical, and Regulatory stakeholders.

The successful candidate will bring strong business acumen, creativity, and the ability to thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment while contributing to the successful development and launch of innovative wound care solutions.

Become a product expert in soft tissue healing and effectively articulate the features and benefits of Restrata to healthcare professionals and sales representatives.

Understand, manage, and develop programs for assigned surgical specialties, including the overall clinical landscape and strategic positioning of Solventum products within each specialty. Build, maintain, and support relationships with key opinion leaders (KOLs) in assigned specialties.

Develop and deliver training programs to educate customer-facing teams on product offerings, ensuring a deep understanding across the organization. Provide technical support for RHT products as needed. Regularly participate in surgeon visits, conferences, and trade shows to represent Solventum and gather voice-of-customer insights.

Collaborate with the graphic design team to develop product collateral, including case studies, brochures, website content, and videos. Partner with cross-functional teams on product specifications and market launches, contributing strategic insights to support business growth.

Conduct customer research through surveys, focus groups, and field visits to identify opportunities for product enhancements and innovation. Monitor market trends and the competitive landscape, providing actionable intelligence to support product development and market positioning.

Your Skills and Expertise: To set you up for success in this role from day one, Solventum requires (at a minimum) the following qualifications: Bachelor’s degree or higher. Three (3) years of experience in sales, marketing, or business management within healthcare, medical devices, or other FDA-regulated industries.

Additional qualifications that could help you succeed even further in this role include: MBA degree or higher from an accredited university Knowledge and experience in advanced wound care or orthopedic, plastic reconstruction, vascular markets and therapies.

Strong communication skills, both written and spoken Demonstrated experience managing projects with multi-disciplinary teams. Independent and strategic thinker able to make solid business decisions Ability to thrive in action oriented high accountability environment. Track record of collaborating cross-functionally that deliver results.

Work location: Remote USA Travel: May include up t o 30-40% predominantly domestic travel (international travel on occasion) Relocation Assistance: Not Authorized Must be legally authorized to work in country of employment without sponsorship for employment visa status (e.g., H1B status).

Sunday Natural emerged from a long-standing passion and research in the fields of health, healing, and personal growth. The lack of natural, high-quality products on the market was the original motivation for founding Sunday Natural in 2013.

We aim to produce the products we ourselves would love to buy – as natural as possible, absolutely pure, free from any additives, and of the highest quality. In a strategic partnership with CVC, Sunday Natural is now one of Germany's most renowned quality manufacturers, with its own research and development department in Berlin.

For the continuous improvement of our products, we collaborate with selected research institutes, scientists, therapists, farmers, and professional associations.
We take our ecological responsibility very seriously: that’s why the majority of our product range is vegan. We also take an innovative approach to packaging: most of our products are packaged in glass, making them almost entirely recyclable.
Our diverse team in Berlin consists of over 350 employees from more than 45 nationalities and continues to grow – but at a sustainable pace. Our goal is to foster a collaborative, supportive, and inclusive work environment with a diverse group of motivated, talented, and visionary team members.

About Netholabs
Netholabs builds large-scale neural and behavioural recording platforms to generate the data needed for the next generation of brain models. We operate two recording platforms: a preclinical ethological monitoring system integrated with behaviour and neural data and a human motion-capture and neurophysiology platform. We are a small, fast-moving team where hardware, neuroscience, and ML sit in the same room.

We are building integrated human motion-capture and neurophysiological recording systems for both controlled lab studies and naturalistic, in-the-wild data collection. Today we have working prototypes. We need someone to turn them into products - reproducible, manufacturable, remotely updatable systems that can be deployed at scale and maintained without an engineer in the room.
You will own R&D delivery across the London lab and hardware programme: co-developing the hardware with our electronics and mechanical engineers, importing and enforcing best-practice data capture protocols, and engaging contract manufacturers to scale. This is an agentic, hands-on role -with support engineer roles as required. You will spend as much time in the lab and on the phone with suppliers as you will in a spec document.

Take working prototypes to shippable, field-deployable systems — define the product, own the roadmap, and drive it to delivery
Specify and build out over-the-air update infrastructure: firmware, versioning, rollback, fleet management, remote diagnostics
Own the design-for-manufacture transition — DFM/DFA reviews, BOM ownership, tolerancing, test fixtures, and production test protocols
Identify, qualify, and manage contract manufacturers and suppliers; own the relationship from RFQ through NPI to sustained production
Establish and enforce best-practice data capture protocols across modalities (EEG, fNIRS, EMG, pupillometry, motion capture, video) so that data quality is consistent across sessions, operators, and sites
Define the requirements that make in-the-wild collection viable: wearability, session setup time, robustness, battery life, and unattended operation
Work directly with our electronics, mechanical, firmware, and neuroscience teams to translate research needs into hardware requirements — and push back when a requirement doesn't survive contact with manufacturing
Build the quality, documentation, and regulatory groundwork (design history, ISO 13485-style discipline, CE/UKCA pathway) appropriate to a research-device product
Contribute to the industrialisation of our rodent recording platform where the manufacturing and OTA problems overlap

Essential
Min 3+ years (ideal 7+) in hardware product management, product engineering, or programme management, with several products you personally took from prototype to volume manufacture
Direct, demonstrable experience with contract manufacturers: you have run RFQs, sat through NPI builds, argued about yield, and fixed a production line problem from 6,000 miles away
Deep understanding of connected-device architecture: OTA update mechanisms, device provisioning, telemetry, fleet management, and what it costs to get these wrong
Fluency across electronics, mechanical, and firmware enough to hold a real technical conversation with each - you don't need to design the board, but you need to know when the answer you're getting is wrong
Track record of writing specifications and protocols that people actually follow
Comfort with ambiguity and a small-company reality: no PMO, no roadmap tooling team, no one to delegate the boring parts to

Experience with wearable, biosignal, or medical device hardware
Familiarity with human research data collection — protocols, participant handling, IRB/ethics, GDPR and special-category data

Background in neuroscience, biomedical engineering, or a related field
Experience with multi-sensor time synchronisation and the data infrastructure behind it

Direct ownership of a product line at a company small enough that your decisions ship

A team of neuroscientists and engineers doing genuinely novel work
Central London lab, on-site, with access to the Sussex rodent facility

Sometimes that's personalisation. Sometimes authentication. Sometimes embedding AI into exactly the right moment in the patient journey. You'll figure that out, own the roadmap, and ship it. Build a tech stack that launches a new market in weeks, not months

### **V-ZUG Procurement** ###
Der Bereich Procurement verantwortet die strategische Beschaffung von Materialien, Komponenten und Dienstleistungen entlang der gesamten Wertschöpfungskette. Als Schweizer Premiumhersteller mit eigener Produktion am Hauptsitz in Zug stellen wir hohe Anforderungen an unsere Lieferanten - und an uns selbst.

Unser Einkauf ist entsprechend professionell aufgestellt: mit klaren Kategorienstrukturen, einem internationalen Lieferantennetzwerk und dem Anspruch, nicht nur Kosten zu optimieren, sondern Partnerschaften zu gestalten, die langfristig tragen.
### **Das bietet dir die Stelle** ###
* Du entwickelst und setzt die Warengruppen- und Lieferantenstrategie für deine Kategorien um - nicht als Verwaltungsaufgabe, sondern als echte Gestaltungsaufgabe: Du entscheidest, welche Lieferanten V-ZUG langfristig begleiten, wo neue Quellen erschlossen werden und wie die Materialversorgung auch in einem volatilen Markt stabil bleibt
* Du steuerst dein Lieferantenportfolio über den gesamten Lebenszyklus - von der Auswahl neuer Partner über gezielte Weiterentwicklung bis zur Ausphasung. Gemeinsam mit dem Supplier Quality Management sorgst du dafür, dass Anspruch und Realität übereinstimmen - durch regelmässige Bewertungen und Audits, die mehr sind als ein Pflichtprogramm
* Du verantwortest das Vertragsmanagement in deinen zugewiesenen Warengruppen im Bereich Mechanik - von der Erstellung über die Verhandlung bis zur laufenden Pflege. Du weisst, was in einem Vertrag wirklich zählt, und bringst interne Stakeholder auf einen gemeinsamen Nenner
* Du führst Ausschreibungen durch, vergleichst Angebote und entwickelst gemeinsam mit den Fachbereichen fundierte Vergabeempfehlungen und Entscheidungen, die wirtschaftliche und technische Anforderungen optimal vereinen
* Du hast die Kostenentwicklung deiner Vorserien- und Serienartikel im Griff: Du erkennst Potenziale frühzeitig, nutzt sie konsequent und setzt Massnahmen um, die nachhaltig wirken
* Du bist fester Bestandteil von Projekten, koordinierst Materialbedarfe mit Lieferanten und stellst sicher, dass Muster, Prototypen und Serienmaterialien dann da sind, wenn sie gebraucht werden
### **Das bringst du für die Stelle mit** ###
* Du hast ein abgeschlossenes Studium in Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen, Betriebswirtschaft, Supply Chain Management oder einer vergleichbaren Disziplin
* Du bringst mehrjährige Erfahrung im Einkauf mit und weisst, wie man Lieferanten gegenüber souverän Position bezieht - mit Verhandlungsgeschick, das nicht laut sein muss, um zu wirken, und einer Kommunikation, die intern wie extern ankommt
* Du denkst strategisch und analytisch: Du erkennst Marktdynamiken, leitest daraus konkrete Massnahmen ab und entwickelst Einkaufsstrategien, die nicht nur für heute, sondern für morgen tragen
* Du weisst, wofür du stehst und bringst die Klarheit, Durchsetzungsstärke und Überzeugungskraft mit, um das auch zu zeigen: im internen Projektumfeld genauso wie im Gespräch mit externen Partnern
* Der sichere Umgang mit ERP-Systemen, insbesondere SAP, sowie digitalen Tools ist für dich selbstverständlich - kein Aufwand, sondern Arbeitsgrundlage
* Du kommunizierst sicher auf Deutsch und Englisch - schriftlich wie mündlich, klar und mit dem richtigen Gespür dafür, was dein Gegenüber braucht

In just five years, Stora has become the platform behind more than 30% of UK self storage locations, and we're scaling globally from here. Operators have processed over £150m in automated payments through us, and see an average of 32% business growth after they switch.
We're doing this in a market that's wide open. Europe has over 10,000 self storage sites and is growing fast, yet it sits years behind the US on maturity and is still barely touched by good software. The UK is our stronghold. The rest of Europe is where we're heading next.
Stora is the operating system for modern self storage: online bookings, payments, facility management, reporting, and automation in one platform. We started as operators ourselves, and that's still how we think. If you want to own a product operators depend on every day, in a company genuinely rethinking how it builds, this is it.
Why this role matters
We have a strong product team, great engineers, and a growing product. The bottleneck isn't ideas or execution capacity. It's people who can hold the full picture at once.
What the business needs, what the customer actually experiences, what's technically feasible, what to cut when time is short, and knowing when to slow down. Making good calls across all of it. That's the job.
We've shortened the loop between insight and shipped product by stripping out the layers that slow good judgement down. The quality bar didn't move. This role exists to keep doing that. It carries real ownership from day one, and the scope grows as Stora does.
The surface you'd own
This is the product operators live in every day, and the storefront their own customers book through. You're designing for two users at once: the operator running the business, and the end customer renting the unit. Getting that B2B2C experience right is a genuine craft problem. It's a broad, central surface, and it's heavy on UX.

Core workflows: customers, units, tenancies, access
Roles, permissions, account structure
Operational reporting: occupancy, utilisation, activity
The internal data layer: event tracking, core models, metric definitions
The growth surface: storefront, checkout, the lead → booking funnel
If an operator uses it daily, or relies on it to understand their business, it sits with this team.
How we actually work
We've changed how product gets built at Stora. This is how we operate now.
Designers work directly in the codebase. Engineers and product people work closely together from the start. We use AI genuinely: to explore, prototype and move faster. The work gets closer to reality, sooner.
If you're at a company that talks about moving faster but runs the same process it did three years ago, this will feel different. We're not done evolving how we work, and this person will have real scope to shape that.

Own a problem space end-to-end, from understanding the customer need to something live in the product
Work across both sides of the experience: operator back office and end-customer storefront
Work directly with engineering leads. Close collaboration, not handoff
Make scope calls. Know what to cut, what's fundamental, what can wait
Work with or without a designer, depending on the problem. What matters is the outcome
Stay close to customers, talk to operators, understand how they run their businesses, bring that into every decision
Shape how we work. The process isn't fixed. If something's slowing things down, fix it

Real product experience at a SaaS company. You've owned features or problem spaces end-to-end and shipped things people use. Roughly 2+ years, though we care more about the evidence than the number
A builder by instinct. You make things: side projects, tools, a company you tried to start. We'd rather see someone who ships than someone who only plans
A design or engineering past works too. You may have come from design, engineering, or somewhere else entirely. Designers and people who've started their own things tend to do well here
Great product taste. You can tell the difference between a solution that works and one that just ships
You define it yourself. You don't need everything defined to make progress
Real design sense. Strong enough to contribute or push back, which matters a lot on a surface this UX-heavy
AI-native. You use AI as a natural part of how you think and work. Not waiting to be shown how
This role is not for you if
You need a detailed brief before you can start
You've only ever worked inside someone else's process and haven't shipped anything of your own
You think good product work stops before it ships
You go quiet when a problem is ambiguous instead of pushing into it
Why Stora

About the opportunity at Beamery
We are looking for an experienced Senior Product Manager to own Beamery's Data Foundry end to end. The Data Foundry is our proprietary data platform, powering existing and emerging product lines including our Talent CRM and Workforce Suite. Through this, we provide data-as-a-service to customers through channels such as MCP/API.

This is an emerging commercial channel. Its core capabilities span the data models, taxonomies and integrations that underpin talent and workforce decisions across our platform.
The Senior Product Manager, Data Foundry will treat data both as infrastructure embedded within our products and as a product that customers buy in its own right. Beyond internal embedding and direct commercial sales, the platform is open — customers and partners can build on top of it through MCP and API access.

You will work with product leadership to set the strategy, agree what the platform provides internally, decide what becomes customer-facing, and define how the platform opens up for customer and partner innovation.
You will work at the centre of the platform, creating a balance between two essential initiatives. On one side, you serve the Talent CRM and Workforce Suite product managers as your customers, agreeing the data contracts they build on. On the other, you partner with the data science, data engineering and integrations engineering leads to turn those needs into delivery.
What you will be doing
Ownership and strategy
Own the Data Foundry vision, strategy and roadmap, framing each item as a bet with a clear driver, aligned to overall strategic objectives
Ensure alignment of Data Foundry strategy to Beamery's AI strategy, reflecting the shift from providing AI assistants to providing AI access through MCP and API channels.
Decide what Data Foundry provides as internal infrastructure and what is packaged and sold as a customer-facing product.
Make and defend build versus buy decisions across integrations, analytics, AI and taxonomy capabilities.
Discovery and commercial impact
Discover and validate what external customers want from data-as-a-service, and partner with Sales and Customer Success to drive adoption with clear GTM and enablement plans
Build the case for Data Foundry as a new commercial channel, defining and proving the standalone commercial model alongside its role as platform foundation, quantify the value it unlocks for specific customers and deals, and measure success against value and usage metrics.
Partnership and delivery
Lead your team to deliver solutions our customers can’t imagine working without and that deliver measurable customer and business outcomes
Agree and maintain the data contracts with the CRM and Workforce Suite product managers, treating them as internal customers with real commitments.
Prioritise across data science, data engineering and integrations engineering, translating tribe needs into a clear and deliverable plan.
Communication & alignment
Communicate transparently and create alignment between peers and leadership on priorities, trade offs and progress
Manage customer and sales expectations through well managed structured cadences
Data governance and trust
Own how workforce data is governed, secured and access-controlled as it is exposed through APIs and MCP, meeting or exceeding enterprise privacy and compliance expectations.
Ensure the outputs of Data Foundry's models are measurable and explainable, so customers and internal teams can trust and act on the results.

A product manager with a minimum 6 years experience in complex technical, data or AI products, a significant portion of which should be in enterprise B2B SaaS.
Strong grasp of data platforms, APIs and integrations, comfortable making architecture-adjacent decisions while collaborating with and holding priorities with engineering and data science leads.
Experience handling sensitive or regulated data, with a clear view of governance, security and privacy.
An analytical thinker who uses data to find opportunities, confidently prioritise and measure success, balancing between competing tribe roadmaps and internal customers.
Commercially fluent, experience with 0-1 product stages, shaping early product with new go to market motions, able to connect product decisions to revenue, cost and customer ROI.
A clear communicator who builds trust across product, data science and engineering, and who is comfortable taking a position and explaining the reasoning.
Experienced owning and delivering AI capabilities, with a keen interest in how AI is reshaping the talent and workforce space, and in giving customers trusted, explainable access to their data.

You will be the person an engineering lead respects for the quality of your requirements, and a credible product voice in front of security customers. You will work on a platform whose unified data model and deployment flexibility, from cloud to on-premises to fully air-gapped, , partnering closely with Engineering and the Elastic Security Labs research team. This is a role for a product manager ready to own meaningful surface area in a fast-moving space and grow toward broader ownership.
What You Will Be Doing
Own a core area of the XDR roadmap end to end: drive detection, correlation, incident building, and response capabilities across endpoint, cloud, identity, and network, from requirements through shipped and iterated product.
Expand and maintain the telemetry and integrations XDR depends on: first-party Elastic data plus third-party EDR, cloud, identity, and network sources that let the product correlate across a real environment.
Contribute to Elastic's exposure and vulnerability management work, including prioritization based on exploitability and reachability rather than raw CVSS, and remediation workflow.
Write requirements engineering can act on without follow-up clarification meetings, and translate customer input and threat research from Elastic Security Labs into product.
Represent product in customer conversations, including senior security stakeholders, and bring what you learn back into the roadmap .
Ensure your capabilities work across Elastic's deployment models, from cloud to on-premises to air-gapped, so they hold up in regulated and disconnected environments.
Maintain well-developed awareness of the competitive landscape and GTM strategies.
Create artifacts such as roadmap trackers and decision memos that give stakeholders visibility without requiring a meeting.

About ABC Legal Services ABC Legal Services is proud to be the national leader in service of process. We are a team of 1000 and growing with offices in Los Angeles, Oklahoma City, Phoenix, Brooklyn, Chicago, Washington DC, and more. Seattle is our home and headquarters.

We've been successful in this unique business for over 30 years and we continue to advance our technology and business processes to remain years ahead of what our competition is able to offer.

Our focus is to expand our technology lead, acquire and integrate less efficient competitors, and tap into new segments through an integrated inbound marketing and sales approach.

ABC Legal is a tech-forward, tech-enabled legal services business — we use technology to power a core operational service, not the other way around. We're hiring a Product Manager to help own one or more of our Service of Process product line: the mobile app process servers use in the field, the customer-facing web portal, the enterprise APIs our largest clients integrate with, and the proprietary platform that powers job assignment, routing, task management, and evidence chain.
Reporting directly to the CTO as a Product Manager, you will own discovery, requirements, cross-functional coordination, launch readiness, and outcome accountability — not backlog grooming and engineering coordination.

You'll work directly with process servers, our operations team, enterprise customers, and engineering, Our product team today sits closer to the execution side of product and is strong at delivery, lighter on discovery, market insight, and outcome ownership. Part of your role is to model what upstream product work looks like at ABC.
Why This Job Is Interesting
Every job we run is a physical-world logistics problem — get a real person to a real address, at a time they'll actually be there. Our product has to serve a distributed field workforce, a demanding set of legal customers, an internal operations organization of hundreds, and a court system that has different rules by county.
We're also further into production AI than almost anyone in this industry: dozens of AI agents run live today across service validation, document handling, evidence review, and operational decision support. You'll help decide where that belongs in the product and where it doesn't.

Process serving is one of the most analog, paper-bound corners of legal services with county-by-county rules, physical proof of service, workflows that haven't changed in decades. We intend to be the company that rebuilds it around AI first, not the one playing catch-up in five years.

You'll help decide what "AI-native" actually means for our business.

Own your product area end to end
Own outcomes, not just output, for your area of the Service of Process product line like the APIs and integrations our largest clients build against, and the proprietary platform behind job assignment, routing, task management, and evidence chain, as well as the customer web portal and our field mobile app.
Set and defend the priority order. Decide what gets built, what waits, and what we stop doing
Maintain a rolling roadmap that survives contact with reality: sequenced, tied to business outcomes, revised openly when the evidence changes.
Run your own discovery
Get into the field. Ride along with process servers, sit with the operations teams who work jobs all day, and watch customers use the product.
Run structured discovery with customers — interviews, win/loss input, support themes, usage data — and turn it into a written point of view about what to build and why.
Serve two distinct user populations: external customers who want speed, price, and certainty, and internal operators whose throughput determines whether we can deliver it.
Turn insight into shipped software
Write the requirements: crisp problem statements, success criteria, edge cases, and the operational and legal constraints that apply by jurisdiction
Own the backlog for your team(s) within our SAFe cadence: features and stories, acceptance, iteration planning, and PI planning.
Work directly and daily with mobile, web, and backend engineering. Break work into releasable increments, unblock decisions fast, and make tradeoff calls
Own launch readiness end to end: rollout plan, internal enablement, support readiness, migration and backfill, and a defined rollback path.
Own release quality for your area. We have no separate QA team: you decide what needs testing and to what depth, shape the test approach, and coordinate the business owners and operations partners who validate the work in their own domain.
Make the go/no-go call, and confirm after release that what shipped does what the requirements said and that the customer and operational outcomes you predicted show up in production.
Partner with Operations as a first-class customer
Treat internal operations as a product surface with real users and real cost. Tooling that saves an ops team minutes per job compounds across hundreds of thousands of jobs
Find where automation, better routing, or better decision support removes manual work — and quantify what that work is worth before committing to it
Ship AI into the product responsibly
ABC runs AI in production today across service validation, evidence review, document handling, and operational decision support. Own where AI belongs in your product area
Define the accuracy bar, the human-review path, and the failure behavior for every AI-assisted feature before it ships. Default to advisory; earn the right to automate by clearing a threshold you set in advance.
Hold AI features to the same outcome accountability as everything else: measured agreement with the qualified human who would otherwise make the call.
Measure, and be accountable to the measurement
Define the success metric for every initiative before it ships, and name the dashboard where it will be watched.
Pull your own numbers. You'll have direct access to our analytics environment and reporting to decide what worked and what didn’t and act on it
Manage risk and compliance
Understand the regulatory and evidentiary texture of this business: jurisdiction- specific service and filing requirements, chain-of-evidence integrity, proof of service standards, and the handling of sensitive case and party data.
Identify compliance and operational risk early and design around it — a product decision that creates a defect in a proof of service is a legal problem, not a bug.
Ensure changes clear the appropriate cross-functional review before release.

4–7 years of product management experience, including at least one product spanning multiple technical surfaces (e.g. mobile + web, or a field/consumer app backed by a core platform).
Demonstrated track record of running your own discovery and turning it into shipped requirements — not just executing a spec you were handed.
Comfortable working directly with engineering across mobile, web, and backend teams simultaneously.
Hands-on backlog ownership in a scaled agile environment — writing and accepting work, running iteration planning, and participating in quarterly planning. SAFe specifically is a plus; scaled agile of some kind is expected.

Product Manager
Full-Time
New York, Chicago or Charlotte
Reports to VP, Central Operations
About Oula
Oula Health is a venture-backed, midwifery-led maternity and GYN care company building the next generation of women's healthcare. We partner exclusively with major health systems — including Mount Sinai, Stamford Health, and Novant Health — to embed our collaborative OB-GYN and midwifery model directly inside their networks. We're a team of ~100 people at Series B stage, with 4 clinics today and three more opening in 2026.

At Oula, our product doesn't sit alongside our EHR — it integrates directly into it. Every product and engineering decision has downstream consequences for how our EHRs are configured, and every EHR configuration decision shapes what's possible on the product side. Someone has to hold both at once.
We're looking for a technically-minded Product Manager to own and evolve our core technology stack — including our EHR, patient portal, and care management platform. This role sits at the intersection of product, operations, and health system integration, serving as the internal and external subject matter expert on our EMR and the primary lead for health system EHR integrations.
You'll manage the day-to-day health of our tech stack, partnering closely with both internal teams and external health system stakeholders to ensure our systems run smoothly and our integrations deliver.

You can sit with a midwife and understand why a clinical template matters, then turn around and write a bug ticket that engineering can actually action, then build the SOP so the next market launch doesn't require you to be in the room. When things are ambiguous (and they often are), you'll lean in rather than wait for clarity.
What You'll Own
EHR Configuration & Clinical Systems
Own day-to-day management of our core tech stack: the EHR, patient portal, and care management platform
Own Athena and Epic configuration end to end: clinical templates, order sets, lab configurations, payer connectivity, and access management for clinical and ops staff
Lead EHR integration efforts as the internal and external subject matter expert — FHIR/HL7 data exchange, health system IT coordination and committed go-live timelines
Own and accelerate Epic integration timelines as we onboard additional health system partners
Maintain configuration integrity as new markets launch and care model workflows evolve
Partner with our IT team on infrastructure; own the clinical systems layer they don't touch
Product Operations & Launch
Own bug intake and prioritization from Market Operations — standardize how Engineering receives, scopes, and resolves issues and communicates status back to the field
Build structured launch toolkits and training materials so clinic teams are prepared for new feature rollouts on day one
Coordinate end-to-end launches across Product, Engineering, and Operations
Identify where AI and automation can reduce manual administrative burden in product operations workflows
Standards & Knowledge Management
Build and maintain the clinical systems SOP library so new market setup is repeatable — documented well enough that a new hire can execute without you in the room
Develop onboarding materials for clinic managers and clinical staff on EHR workflows and tooling
Drive feature parity efforts so patients and clinicians experience a consistent standard of care across markets
Data & Reporting
Build and maintain dashboards tracking feature adoption, issue resolution, and rollout health across clinics
Develop quarterly reporting for Product, leadership, and health system partners on platform performance
Ensure data infrastructure is in place to measure the impact of every feature rollout

3+ years with product operations, technical program management, or PM-adjacent work — ideally at a growth-stage digital health or services company
Strong problem-solving instincts and genuine curiosity — you like figuring out how things work and making them work better
Ease with ambiguity and a bias toward action; this role requires you to create the playbook, not execute someone else's
Demonstrated ability to navigate complex stakeholder environments and drive aggressive timelines — ideally with client-facing or health system-facing experience
Ability to speak ‘multiple languages’ – comfort going deep on technical details while communicating clearly to non-technical audiences; you can write a bug ticket, an SOP, and a launch plan that people actually follow; hands-on EHR configuration and integration experience strongly preferred
Analytical enough to build a dashboard and identify a pattern, even if you're not a SQL expert
What Success Looks Like
In your first 90 days, you've audited our current Athena configuration, identified gaps, and have a remediation plan. You understand the bug triage process well enough to have improved it. You've met your counterparts at every health system partner and know what's coming for the next Epic integration.
At six months, new market launches have a repeatable systems and product checklist. Clinic teams know what to expect before a feature goes live. Bug resolution time is measurably faster and the field is no longer sending issues into a black hole.
At one year, the SOP library is comprehensive, clinical systems configuration is stable and documented, and you've successfully navigated at least one new health system EHR environment. The product team has a reliable partner and the ops team isn't dependent on any single person for systems knowledge.
